# CLI reference: `burroughs`

*Written against `v0.11.0` from `cmd/burroughs/main.go` and `run.go`. Every transcript is generated by this site's
CI: it builds the CLI at the latest release tag (`go build github.com/scttfrdmn/burroughs/cmd/burroughs`), runs the
sessions in `examples/cli/`, and fails if any output differs from what is shown here. `[exit N]` is the exit status
when it is not 0.*

```console title="examples/cli/transcripts/cli-usage.txt"
--8<-- "examples/cli/transcripts/cli-usage.txt"
```

The top-level usage line above lists only `--strict`. `run` takes more flags than that. `burroughs run` with no
file prints the full list.

The `run` subcommand goes through the public Go API and nothing else, so anything it does, an embedder can do too
(decision 0029). `inspect` is the exception: its section dump uses the engine's internal decoder, which has no public equivalent.

## `burroughs version`

Prints a fixed banner and exits 0:

```console title="examples/cli/transcripts/gs-version.txt"
--8<-- "examples/cli/transcripts/gs-version.txt"
```

!!! bug "Known issue: the banner says `v0.0.1` ([#1130](https://github.com/scttfrdmn/burroughs/issues/1130))"
    The banner is a constant. It does **not** report the module version, and says `v0.0.1` even in `v0.11.0`.

## `burroughs inspect file.wasm`

Decodes a **core module** and lists its sections and their sizes. The second command shows it refusing a
component:

```console title="examples/cli/transcripts/cli-inspect.txt"
--8<-- "examples/cli/transcripts/cli-inspect.txt"
```

- It decodes and does not validate. A module that fails *typing* still exits 0, because the section dump is complete.
- A file it cannot decode exits 3 (malformed). A construct from a gated-off proposal exits 6.
- **It does not understand components.** A component is refused as malformed (above).
- It never exits 4 or 5, because nothing it does can trap or reach an unimplemented instruction.

## `burroughs run`

``` { .text .fragment }
burroughs run [--strict] [--dir HOST[:/GUEST]]... [--scratch HOST[:/GUEST]]... [--env NAME[=VALUE]]...
              [--features NAME[,NAME]]... <file.wasm> [-- <arg>...] | [<func> [<value>...]]
```

(That is the first line of `burroughs run`'s usage text, wrapped; the transcript of the two-colon refusal below
shows it as printed.)

### How the file is routed

The bytes decide the path. There is no flag to choose it.

1. **WASI preview 1 command**: a module that imports `wasi_snapshot_preview1` *and* exports `_start`. `_start` is
   run with `argv[0]` set to the file's base name and the arguments after `--` following it. Stdin, stdout and stderr
   are the process's own. The guest's exit code becomes the CLI's exit code.
2. **Component** (the preamble's layer field says component): its `wasi:cli/run` export is run through
   `ComponentConfig.Run`, with the process's stdin, stdout and stderr.
3. **Core module**: instantiated with `Config{Strict: --strict}`. With no function named, its exported functions
   are listed one per line. With a function named, that function is called with the typed values that follow, and
   the results are printed on one line separated by spaces. A function with no results prints nothing.

### Flags

| Flag | Applies to | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--strict` | core modules | Refuse a module the validator could not fully check (exit 3) instead of running it. See [declined](concepts.md#the-vocabulary-trap-refused-declined-unsupported-gated). |
| `--dir HOST[:/GUEST]` | wasip1 | Grant a directory **read-only**. Repeatable. With no `:/GUEST`, the directory is mapped under its own absolute host path. |
| `--scratch HOST[:/GUEST]` | wasip1 | Grant a **writable** directory. Writes are confined beneath it. Repeatable. |
| `--env NAME=VALUE` / `--env NAME` | wasip1 | Put a variable in the guest's environment. A bare `NAME` copies the host's value and is refused if it is unset. Repeatable. **Nothing is passed unless named.** |
| `--features NAME[,NAME]` | wasip1 | Proposal capabilities the guest needs. The only recognized name is `threads`. Anything else is refused (exit 5). **No effect on core modules**, because `Config` has no feature set (an unrecognized name is still refused). On a component it triggers the misrouting described below (#1128). |
| `-- arg...` | wasip1, components | The guest's arguments. |

How `--dir` and `--scratch` are parsed:

- **The separator is one colon**: `--dir ./data:/data`. wasmtime's two-colon form is refused by name. The first
  two lines of the transcript; the full usage text and `[exit 2]` follow:

    ```console title="examples/cli/transcripts/cli-dir-twocolon.txt"
    --8<-- "examples/cli/transcripts/cli-dir-twocolon.txt:1:2"
    ```
- **The guest path must be absolute.** `--dir ./data:data` is refused. A relative guest path would be a grant
  that nothing can open through.
- A refused flag prints the full usage text after the message and exits 2.

What a guest gets by default:

- **The guest's environment is empty** unless you pass `--env`. One thing to know: a Go `wasip1` guest takes its
  working directory from `PWD`, so `--env PWD=/x` changes where its relative paths resolve.
- **`--dir` is read-only.** A write through it fails in the guest with `Capabilities insufficient` (`ENOTCAPABLE`).
- **`--scratch` does not filter what is inside the directory you give it.** Bind mounts, `/proc` and device files
  inside it are reachable. You choose the directory, and confinement only keeps the guest from leaving it
  (ADR 0091).

### Value syntax (core module arguments and results)

| Spelling | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `i32:42`, `i32:-1`, `i32:4294967295`, `i32:0x2a` | i32. The signed and unsigned spellings of one bit pattern are both accepted. |
| `i64:-1` | i64 |
| `f32:1.5`, `f32:nan`, `f32:nan:0x200000`, `f32:inf` | f32. NaN payloads are preserved. |
| `f64:inf`, `f64:nan` | f64 |
| `v128:0x1:0x2` | v128, as low and high 64-bit halves. Printed zero-padded: `v128:0x0000000000000001:0x0000000000000002`. |
| `extern:3` | non-null externref with host identity 3 |
| `null:func`, `null:extern` | null reference of that type |

A result may print as `ref:<payload>:<type>`, for example a GC struct or a funcref. Except for a host reference (`ref:host:N:<type>`, which reads back), those are results only: there is
no argument spelling for them, because a host cannot construct one.

### What does not work for components through the CLI (v0.11.0)

!!! bug "Known issue, to be fixed in `v0.12.0` ([#1128](https://github.com/scttfrdmn/burroughs/issues/1128))"
    `burroughs run` misroutes a component given guest arguments, `--dir` or `--features`, and silently ignores some
    flags per kind. #1128 is on the `v0.12.0` milestone; until it ships, the transcript below is what `v0.11.0`
    does.

```console title="examples/cli/transcripts/cli-component-misrouted.txt"
--8<-- "examples/cli/transcripts/cli-component-misrouted.txt"
```

- **`--` arguments, `--dir` and `--features` on a component produce a misleading "malformed" refusal (exit 3).**
  When any of them is given, `run` first tries to read the file as a `wasip1` command. A component fails that
  decode, and the decode error is returned before the component path is tried (the first three commands above).
  `65549` is `0x0001000d`, a component's version-and-layer word.

  So **a component run from the CLI cannot be given arguments**. A Go embedder can pass them through
  `ComponentConfig.Args`.
- **`--env` and `--scratch` are silently ignored for components** (the fourth command). The component host models
  no environment and no filesystem.
- **`--features` has no effect on a core module.** A name is still checked, so an unrecognized one is refused
  (exit 5, the last command), but `--features=threads` does not re-admit threads for a core module (see
  [tutorial 4](tutorials/04-traps-and-refusals.md#burroughs_threads0)).
- **A component's typed exports cannot be called from the CLI.** Use `Component.Call` from Go.
- **`--strict` has no effect on wasip1 commands or components.** It only affects the core-module path.

## Exit codes

There is one table for the whole CLI, so `inspect` and `run` mean the same thing by each code.

| Code | Meaning | From |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | The module ran. | |
| `1` | This invocation's own failure: an unreadable file, a value with no type prefix, no such export, wrong arity or argument type. | anything unclassified |
| `2` | Wrong arguments to the CLI itself. | usage errors, refused flags |
| `3` | The module was refused: malformed, invalid, declined under `--strict`, or **unlinkable** (an import nothing supplies). | `ErrMalformed`, `ErrInvalid`, `ErrDeclined`, `ErrUnlinkable` |
| `4` | The module executed correctly and the program went wrong: a trap in a core module or a component, or a component call refused because an earlier trap locked the instance. | `*Trap`, `ErrInstanceLocked` |
| `5` | The engine reached something it does not implement in this phase. An unrecognized `--features` name also lands here. | `ErrUnsupported` |
| `6` | The module is fine, but this build has that proposal's gate off. | `ErrGated` |
| `7` | A component call the caller cancelled. | `ErrCancelled` |
| `8` | A call on a component that has been closed. | `ErrComponentClosed` |
| `9` | `Close` reached its bound with a guest still cancelling, and tore down anyway. | `ErrCloseIncomplete` |
| *guest's* | A `wasip1` command or component that exits non-zero passes its own code through. | `proc_exit` / `wasi:cli/exit` |

Codes 7, 8 and 9 **cannot happen through this CLI**: `run` never cancels or closes a component. They exist because
every public sentinel has a code, which the repo checks with `TestExitCodesCoverEveryPublicSentinel`.

Two things to know about the table:

- **A guest's own exit code can collide with these.** A `wasip1` guest that exits 3 is indistinguishable by code
  alone from a refused module. The message on stderr tells them apart: a guest exit prints no `burroughs:` line.
- **The repository README's version of this table leaves out unlinkable modules.** The code (`exitCode` in
  `cmd/burroughs/run.go`) maps `ErrUnlinkable` to 3, and that is what you see (the `imports.wasm` line in
  [tutorial 4](tutorials/04-traps-and-refusals.md#the-same-modules-through-the-cli)). The README's omission is filed
  as [#1130](https://github.com/scttfrdmn/burroughs/issues/1130).

## Environment switches

These environment variables roll back default-on gates. Each is read when it is used, and the only value with any
effect is `0`:

| Variable | Effect of `=0` |
| --- | --- |
| `BURROUGHS_THREADS` | Shared memories and atomics are refused as gated (exit 6). `--features=threads` admits them again for a wasip1 command. Nothing re-admits them for a core module run with a function name. |
| `BURROUGHS_COMPONENTS` | Every component is refused as gated (exit 6). |
| `BURROUGHS_ASYNC` | Components using the async ABI are refused as gated (exit 6). |
| `BURROUGHS_CM_THREADS` | Components using component-model threads are refused as gated. |

`BURROUGHS_NO_SKIP` also exists, but it belongs to the repository's own test suite and has no effect on the CLI.
[Tutorial 4](tutorials/04-traps-and-refusals.md#the-environment-switches) has transcripts.
